paper_metadata.title: Mechanical Performance and Microstructural Evolution of (NiCo)75Cr17Fe8Cx (x = 0~0.83) Medium Entropy Alloys at Room and Cryogenic Temperatures

evidence.quote: We investigated the eﬀects of the addition of Co and carbon on the deformation behavior of new medium-entropy alloys (MEAs) designed by increasing the entropy of the conventional NiCrFe-type Alloy 600.

the composition of the alloys in the present study is similar to that of 600-type (Ni-Cr(14–17 wt.%)-Fe(8–10 wt.%)) alloys except that approximately half of major Ni content (72–80%) was substituted by Co
The carbon content was measured to be 0.34 at.% and 0.83 at.% using a Leco C/S-844 C/S determinator

process_steps.input_state: elemental metals >99.9% purity (Co, Ni, Cr, Fe) and ferrochrome with high carbon content

evidence.quote: Alloy 600-type non-equiatomic NiCoCrFe alloy ingots with carbon addition up to 0.8 at.% were cast using vacuum induction melting using Co, Ni, Cr and Fe of >99.9% purity.
The ingots were then cut into a size of 30 × 40 × 15 mm3 and homogenized at 1200 ◦C for 6 h in a vacuum, followed by cooling in air.
After homogenization, the ingots were rolled into plates with a thickness of 1 mm at room temperature.
In order to obtain an alloy with a recrystallized microstructure, the rolled plates were annealed at 850 ◦C for 1 h.

attributes.morphology: homogeneously distributed with slight tendency of dislocation clustering

evidence.quote: In carbon free (NiCo) 75Cr17Fe8 alloy, a rather homogeneously distributed dislocation structure with a slight tendency of dislocation clustering was observed.

mechanisms.name: grain boundary pinning by carbide particles

evidence.quote: The decrease of grain size with increase of carbon content in (NiCo)75Cr17Fe8Cx MEAs is attributed to grain boundary pinning effect of carbide particles

The concurrent recrystallization and precipitation of submicron carbides at twin and grain boundaries during annealing at 850 ◦C eﬀectively prohibited the grain growth, resulting in a signiﬁcant increase in strength, which can be predicted by the Hall–Petch equation.
Strengthening by submicron carbide precipitation caused by the passage of dislocations through non-shearable particles can be predicted by an Ashby–Orowan type equation

The strengthening component due to interstitial solution eﬀect by using the interstitial carbon content was calculated to be 4.9 MPa and 10.2 MPa at room temperature and 7.4 MPa and 15.2 MPa at cryogenic temperature, respectively
In carbon-free (NiCo)75Cr17Fe8, the friction stress component consisting of the intrinsic stress and the solid solution strengthening increases signiﬁcantly with the decrease of temperature

The excellent strength and ductility of (NiCo) 75Cr17Fe8 at cryogenic temperature is attributed to the increased strain hardening rate caused by the interaction between dislocation slip and deformation twins.
